newsitem.title: USA: Sprint to test prison videoconferencing.
newsitem.headline: Sprint to test prison videoconferencing.

text.p: Sprint Corp, working with the State of Missouri, said Tuesday it will launch a one-year study involving a videoconferencing program for state prison inmates and their families.

The telecommunications services provider said family members and attorneys of inmates will be able to visit through two-way teleconferences from remote public sites. The pilot program is expected to save travel costs for families, make visitation easier and improve inmate security, Sprint said.
Sprint said it will make the arrangements to schedule the visits and families will pay a special rate for the service.
Videoconferencing equipment will be installed at three state prisons in Missouri within 60 days, Sprint said.
Sprint shares were off 3/16 Tuesday at 45-13/16.
